review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue the cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. A new, sharply focused paper on verified lossless action search for analytically integrated neural continuations could merit evaluation after the computational contribution is isolated, stress-tested, and compared with optimized conventional implementations.

independent_review_execution.mode: Embedded arithmetic was executed from values pinned to RESULT_AUDIT59 and the committed tables; the script also supports full-repository verification.

blocking_findings: The generic screen is an elementary finite-lattice interval exclusion rule, while the useful exact reduction is specialized to scalar actions, one-layer affine-ReLU continuations, scalar uniform innovations, and a quartic primitive objective.
Every production neural query retains exactly one lattice point and no fallback occurs, so the catalogue does not identify survivor, tie, precision, width, lattice, seed, or fallback frontiers.
The comparison changes exact ridge reduction, vectorization, interval screening, enumeration, and root-isolation behavior jointly and lacks a factorial implementation ablation.
Complete-process gains are modest, one paired repetition reverses the ranking, CPU frequency is uncontrolled, and task groups use different runners.
The exact fitted witness changes only one printed R58 datewise decision and has not produced a certified lower policy cost in the retained fresh comparisons.
Common-only is fastest in all six retained R57 task-target groups and exact ReLU is slower in all six; the within-neural speedup does not establish method selection against conventional controls.
Representative all-state Bellman-policy-loss bounds remain approximately 3.95, 6.78, and 9.25 while the successful service stops on an initial-law installed-policy cost target.
The complexity account omits rational operand bit lengths, interval precision, vectorization, memory traffic, and a crossover analysis against other certified optimization methods.
The computation-price identity is uncalibrated and the recorded saving is not shown to change an economically substantive adoption decision.
The 107-page active paper and much larger complete companions remain disproportionate to the narrow lossless scalar-action solver contribution.
positive_findings: R59 is a canonical, clean-rebuildable, source-bound review object.
The lossless screening theorem appears internally coherent under its stated interval and exact-evaluation assumptions.
The solver preserves exact policy identity, tie rules, certificates, path endpoints, and prospective stopping transcripts.
The matched work boundary includes fitting, search, verification, inference, output, and process termination.
Machine-independent operation counts explain the observed reduction in exact evaluations and root isolation.
Budget exhaustion remains failure rather than successful target attainment.
Identical-policy welfare and computation charges are kept separate.
Earlier adverse conventional comparisons and unresolved policy-cost results are retained.

limitations: The reviewer did not retrain, resimulate, or retime the services; new execution would create new observations.
The audit checks frozen summaries, arithmetic, committed tables, and selected service semantics; it is not an independent proof of every inherited theorem.
Single-host and uncontrolled-frequency clocks support descriptive finite-workload comparisons, not hardware-general inference.
No claim is made that common-only or another conventional method dominates outside the declared R57 and R58 tasks.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
